writeup: TIC 182463007 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.3823 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The system shows a primary eclipse with a depth of 9.47 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The eclipse signal achieved a high detection significance with a BLS signal-to-noise ratio of 729.4, and pixel-level analysis confirmed the signal with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 123.9, though the centroid offset measured 5.4 arcseconds from the target position. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning pipeline assigned it a screening score of 0.58, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a genuine binary system. The candidate passed all data quality checks.
